# Trajectory distillation: separate sampler, proposal, and divergence direction

[简体中文](../../../../learning/deep-dives/post-training/student-trajectory-distillation.md) · English

Updated 2026-11-05 · 43 topic entries / 9 representative comparisons

On-policy describes supervised states; FKL/RKL/JSD describe how distributions compare there. GKD and MiniLLM establish those axes, DrOPD and AP-OPD adjust correction location or strength, and Semi-OPD and learning-signal diagnostics distinguish offline reuse from residual loss. MPOPD adds a learnable proposal. Its geometric-mixture target differs from the student's teacher-directed RKL.

[Mechanisms](#comparison) · [Trade-offs](#analysis) · [Cross-paper questions](#questions) · [Updates](#updates)

!!! note "How to read this card"

    The table compares representative methods. It is not a shared-benchmark leaderboard. Teaching examples are not measured results.

## Trade-off analysis {#analysis}

### Student trajectories can still support different learning directions

GKD supervises prefixes students actually visit but permits multiple divergences. MiniLLM chooses student-to-teacher RKL, which may weakly correct teacher options with very low student support. DrOPD retains RKL and adds FKL only on high-divergence positions over joint candidate support. State sampling, divergence direction, and updated candidates need separate checks.

Sources: [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md) · [Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en.md)

### Large loss, weak gradients, and spikes are not one fault

OPD Learning Signals logs losses and gradients jointly rather than treating residual discrepancy as strong learning potential. AP-OPD scales whole blocks after abrupt penalty rises without changing signs; it does not explain plateaus generally. Semi-OPD changes state reuse; fixed teacher labels do not freeze student-dependent advantages.

Sources: [Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals](../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en.md) · [Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en.md) · [When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better](../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en.md)

### A new sampler does not make the geometric mixture the student target

GKD supervises student prefixes and MiniLLM chooses student-to-teacher RKL. MPOPD keeps the teacher target but learns a separate proposal for reachability. The geometric mixture trains only the proposal. Correct sampling mismatch with the frozen old-student/old-proposal one-step ratio from the previous token, not a trajectory product. A real system must reset from the updated student each round; external logits alone do not establish trajectory provenance.

Sources: [Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md)

### A fixed outer reference can contain current-policy inner branches

GKD/MiniLLM supervise student-visited states; MPOPD adds an independently trained proposal to change reachability. SpecOPD instead targets speculative drafters: fixed reference anchors host freshly sampled inner branches, removing full-response verification dependencies. Fixed reference does not make these branches off-policy, but neither is this unrestricted student generation. E2E-TV needs full teacher mass and private predecessor histories. Passing its loss checks proves neither hybrid-target state sharing nor faster serving.

Sources: [SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding](../../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en.md)

### Even on student trajectories, the problem condition changes which states are visited

GKD supervises prefixes actually visited by the student without requiring one unique divergence. Shuffled OPSD makes the shared problem a design variable: the same T(x) determines both student sampling and teacher scoring, while a fixed unrelated reference appears only in the teacher. Shuffling only teacher inputs or generated continuations changes that structure. Its signed pointwise cap retains negatives rather than ordinary KL, so a negative total can be intentional. State source, shared input, privileged context and the numerical objective remain separate checks; passing a local loss test does not establish mathematical improvement.

Sources: [Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?](../../../../post-training/2611.04958-shuffled-opsd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md)

## Cross-paper questions {#questions}

Try answering before expanding the explanation. Each question relates at least two papers.

### If a SpecOPD branch diverges after its reference anchor, should the teacher still score using the reference suffix? {#cross-branch-prefix-is-not-reference-label}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The teacher conditions on the reference prefix and the branch's sampled predecessors, not the reference continuation, future tokens, or siblings. The anchor predicts the first sample; predecessor rows predict later ones. Changing this history or reading the token's own row changes the method and can leak the answer.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: With reference a quiet and draft short evening, evening is predicted from a short, not a quiet, and must not be supplied as its own input first.

    Sources: [SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding](../../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md)

### Why add FKL in DrOPD if GKD and MiniLLM already learn along student trajectories? {#cross-on-policy-not-one-kl}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Student trajectories determine prefixes only. MiniLLM RKL favors teacher modes the student supports, so low-probability teacher candidates can receive weak correction. DrOPD routes extra FKL at high-JS positions and retains teacher support. It does not change sampler or add unlimited FKL everywhere.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: A student considers only A at a visited mistaken prefix while a teacher favors B. Visiting the prefix does not guarantee a useful correction toward B.

    Sources: [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md) · [Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en.md)

### Why cache Semi-OPD teacher scores but not teacher-minus-student advantages forever? {#cross-frozen-teacher-versus-student-score}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Teacher configuration is fixed, but student parameters and log-probabilities change, so recompute differences. Stale advantages respond to old errors. Semi-OPD also fixes initial trajectories unlike continuously sampled GKD; neither implies all probabilities stay constant.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: An old teacher advantage can keep pushing a token the student has already learned.

    Sources: [When Do We Need On-Policy Distillation? Distilling on Offline Student Rollouts Is Often Better](../../../../post-training/2610.11291-semi-opd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md)

### Are AP-OPD spike damping and DrOPD high-divergence FKL opposite corrections? {#cross-spike-versus-direction-repair}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** They detect different things. AP-OPD checks neighboring raw penalty blocks and scales all signed coefficients; DrOPD detects JS divergence and undercoverage and adds a direction. Strength and composition differ.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: Persistent high divergence with no jump can trigger DrOPD but not AP-OPD; their gates are not complementary thresholds.

    Sources: [Adaptive Pullback: Reweighting Supervision at Penalty Jumps in On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.28194-ap-opd/README-en.md) · [Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models](../../../../post-training/2610.19572-divergence-routed-opd/README-en.md) · [Why On-Policy Distillation Sometimes Fails: Vanishing Learning Signals](../../../../post-training/2610.11247-opd-learning-signals/README-en.md)

### Should MPOPD distill the proposal's teacher–student mixture directly into the student? {#cross-mpopd-proposal-target-versus-student-target}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** No. The mixture shapes proposal sampling; the student still learns RKL to the teacher. Student loss uses a frozen old-student versus old-proposal single-step ratio with one-token lag. This adds a proposal axis beyond sampled states and divergence direction.

    **Illustrative example:** Illustration: A proposal can reach a teacher-supported prefix more often without replacing the teacher target by a compromise.

    Sources: [Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md)

### Does shuffling the problem in Shuffled OPSD make supervision off-policy under GKD's student-trajectory principle? {#cross-shared-input-shuffle-not-offpolicy}

??? note "Show answer and example"

    **Answer:** Not by itself. If the student actually samples from the transformed shared problem and the teacher scores that same problem and sampled prefix, supervision still concerns student-visited states. Changed training inputs, teacher-only references and the capped objective remain separate issues. Caching intact-problem trajectories and changing only the teacher's problem breaks condition alignment.

    **Illustrative example:** Teaching example: The student samples y from coins red five contains box and the teacher scores the same T(x),y prefix. A student that actually saw the intact problem paired with a teacher seeing the shuffled one is a different condition.

    Sources: [Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?](../../../../post-training/2611.04958-shuffled-opsd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md)

## Update log {#updates}

Updates record new approaches, changed trade-offs, and follow-up evidence.

**2026-11-05** · Adds Shuffled OPSD's shared-problem transformation against GKD's student-visited-prefix principle, separating fixed reference pairing, signed upper capping and intact-problem evaluation without calling input perturbation or L1 gradients a capability reproduction.

Affected: [Shuffled OPSD: When Semantic Consistency Hurts On-Policy Self-Distillation?](../../../../post-training/2611.04958-shuffled-opsd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md)

**2026-11-04** · Reviewed SpecOPD, separating the fixed outer reference, current-draft inner branches, and E2E-TV. Adds collection dependencies beyond GKD/MPOPD, retaining full teacher mass, ancestry isolation, and predecessor readout without calling L1 tensor checks serving speedup.

Affected: [SpecOPD: Branch-Parallel On-Policy Distillation for Speculative Decoding](../../../../post-training/2611.02846-specopd/README-en.md)

**2026-10-30** · Reviewed MPOPD v2, separating proposal, student RKL, teacher top-k support, and the frozen single-step ratio lagged one token. Adds a learnable sampler axis beyond GKD/MiniLLM and preserves prerequisites such as proposal reset.

Affected: [Proposing Better Rollouts for On-Policy Distillation](../../../../post-training/2610.36477-mpopd/README-en.md) · [GKD](../../../../post-training/2306.13649-gkd/README-en.md) · [MiniLLM](../../../../post-training/2306.08543-minillm/README-en.md)

**2026-10-27** · Initial edition: separates student state distributions and divergence, comparing GKD/MiniLLM, DrOPD/AP-OPD, Semi-OPD, and learning-signal diagnostics; 40 abstracts and six close reads.
